main_body: Orange-red tree canopy (a lumpy mound, rows 1-28) on a thin brown trunk (rows 29-44)
top_band: none: the column at x=23 runs outline (row 1), mid-red (rows 2-4), one light pixel (row 7), then mid-red (rows 8-14). No distinct lighter horizontal surface sits above a front face with a step of 25 L or more.
evidence: The canopy is a speckled blob with no readable top surface separated from a front face. The L values in the canopy columns jump around between 37, 58, 83 and 112 as noise, not as a top band followed by a step and a face. The trunk is a flat vertical strip drawn straight from the front, and it has no visible top or base surface. Under the strict rule, a body with no distinct top band fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile. The references have 427 and 567 colours and a median of about 108 per tile. The canopy has about 5 red-orange steps but they are scattered as noise rather than shaped into leaf clumps. The trunk has only 2-3 browns with a near-black navy outline. 28% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is partly dark red-brown and partly neutral dark. It is much thinner and flatter than the Beodeul trees, which have layered clumps, branch structure and roots.
